title: Express.js Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Reply to a request
entries.summary: A route pairs a method and path with a function. Open GET / to receive this text.
notes: The method and path must both match the route.

entries.name: Send structured data
entries.summary: JSON is a text format for named data. GET /book returns a small object.
notes: Use res.json for data so Express sets the JSON content type.

entries.name: Read part of a path
entries.summary: A colon marks a path input. GET /hello/Ravi places Ravi in req.params.name.
notes: Path inputs arrive as text; do not trust them as numbers automatically.

entries.name: Read a query value
entries.summary: Query values follow ? in a URL. Visit GET /search?q=cat to read q.
notes: A query value can have an unexpected shape; check it before use.

entries.name: Read a JSON body
entries.summary: POST can send a body. Send POST /books with Content-Type application/json and body {"title":"Moon Trip"}.
notes: express.json must run before routes that read a JSON body.

entries.name: Check a number
entries.summary: A route value needs checks before maths. GET /double/4 returns a doubled whole number.
notes: Number() can fail or produce decimals; check the allowed kind of value.

entries.name: Run a shared step
entries.summary: Middleware runs before a later handler when it calls next. GET / shows the value this middleware placed in res.locals.
notes: Middleware must send a response or call next; otherwise the request waits.

entries.name: Group related routes
entries.summary: A Router groups routes under a shared prefix. GET /api/books uses both the prefix and inner path.
notes: The mounted prefix is part of the final URL.

entries.name: Say when an item is missing
entries.summary: A status code tells the client what happened. GET /books/99 returns 404 because this practice item is absent.
notes: Set the status before sending the response body.

entries.name: Point to another route
entries.summary: A redirect asks the client to visit another URL. GET /start points to /hello; a browser follows it.
notes: A redirect is a new request, not an internal function call.

entries.name: Handle a route error
entries.summary: An error handler has four inputs. GET /broken throws an error, which the last handler turns into a clear reply.
notes: Place error middleware after the routes and avoid exposing private error details.

entries.name: Handle an unknown path
entries.summary: A final middleware can reply when no earlier route matched. GET /missing reaches this fallback.
notes: Put the fallback last so it does not hide real routes.
